text.p: French broker SGE Delahaye has upgraded Compagnie de Suez to outperform from neutral, citing a clearer view of the holding company's business following its sale of property loans, fund managers said on Tuesday.
The broker revised the forecast 1997 earnings per share to 17.7 francs from 15.4.
Suez shares closed up 6.94 percent at 248 francs, while the market was up 1.95 percent.
Even if rumours of a link up between Suez and utilities firm Lyonnaise des Eaux did not prove true, the upgrade was justified because of the asset sales, the broker said.

Suez said on Monday it has sold a portfolio of property loans for three billion francs to U.S. investment fund Whitehall, managed by Goldman Sachs. Suez is taking a one billion franc charge on the disposal.
Suez expects to make a 1996 net profit of 800 million francs after the charge.
